articleTitle: Ba-Ferrite Films Prepared by Sol-Gel Pyrolysis Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Crystallographic and magnetic properties of Ba-ferrite films prepared by a sol-gel pyrolysis method were investigated. A solution of Ba- and Fe-nitrates dissolved in ethylene glycol became a gel with an appropriate viscosity by ultrasonic stirring at 80°C. Films were spin-coated onto SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Si substratesr dried and then heated in air at various temperatures. In films prepared at a composition ratio of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Ba=5, a drying temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub>=250°C and a crystallizing temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub>=800°C, single-phase Ba-ferrite was obtained, and the magnetization at 10 kOe field σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10k</sub> and coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> were 47.0 emu/g and 3 ~ 4 kOe, respectively. Films prepared at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub>=250°C had smooth surfaces without any cracks. In thin films of thickness 900Å, preferred orientation of the c-axis was observed.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Microcrystalline Fe-M-C (M = V,Nb,Ta) Films with High Thermal Stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic and structural properties of microcrystalline Fe-M-C (M = V, Nb, Ta) alloy films prepared by annealing sputter-deposited amorphous films were investigated. These new alloys are composed of α-Fe and M carbides with grain diameters of less than 10 nm. Good soft magnetic properties and high saturation flux densities of up to 1.6 T were obtained for Fe-Nb-C and Fe-Ta-C films. Suppression of the growth of α-Fe grains by fine carbide particles resulted in high thermal stability. In particular, Fe-Ta-C films exhibited a low coercive force, less than 65 A/m, even after annealing at 973 K. It was found that the magnetostriction of Fe-M-C films depends on the film composition and annealing temperature. Zero-magnetostrict ive Fe-Ta-C films with permeabilities as high as 5000 (|μ|<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1MHz</sub>) were obtained at various annealing temperatures (823 to 923 K) by controlling the film composition.

articleTitle: Formation of Ni-Zn-Ferrite Films Using Laser Ablation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Ni-Zn-ferrite thin films were formed on glass substrate by a laser ablation method employing a KrF excimer laser at wave-length 248 nm and frequency 15 Hz. Film was deposited on substrate at room temperature, 200°C and 350°C, to a thickness of 2 μm. Ni-Zn-ferrite films thus prepared had the spinel structure when the substrate temperature was raised to 200°C. The saturation magnetic flux densities of Ni-Zn-ferrite films annealed at 400°C were between 1300 and 2020 G. The coercive force of annealed Ni-Zn-ferrite films decreased from 534 to from 70 to 113 Oe as the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O gas pressure was decreased from 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Torr to 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> Torr.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bi-Substituted YIG Garnets by Sol-Gel Synthesis and Their Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bi, Al-substituted YIG was synthesized by the sol-gel method using a solution of yttrium, iron, bismuth and aluminum nitrates dissolved in ethylene glycol. Films were fabricated by spin-coating a gel solution onto glass substrate. The film thickness was controlled by repeating the spin-coating several times. Coated films were subjected to heat treatment in air at 700°C for 4 hours to obtain YIG crystal. The magnetization of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> lies in the plane of the film. Films magnetized normal to the film plane were obtained at a composition of Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.8</inf>A1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>, but the magnetization tends to incline toward the film plane with increasing film thickness. This may be explained in terms of the stress due to substrate constraint: stress relief becomes significant as the film thickness is increased by repeated spin-coating. This can, to a great extent, be eliminated by heat treatment after each spin coating. The magneto-optical Faraday rotation in films is compared for films annealed after the completion of spin-coatings, and films annealed after each spin-coating.

articleTitle: Absolute Value Measurements of Thin Film Permeability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for highly precise measurement of the permeability of thin films in the VHF frequency range has been developed. The permeability of a film sample in a strong magnetic field can be predicted with very high accuracy; this permeability is then used as the standard of a measurement system. Multilayer films with various spacer thicknesses and a FeZrN micro-crystalline film were measured. Results showed that eddy current losses in the multilayer films cannot be suppressed even with insulating spacers as thick as 2000Å, and that the micro-crystalline film exhibits relatively high losses in the high-frequency range.

articleTitle: Measurement of Iron Loss Using Rotational Magnetic Loss Measurement Apparatus
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Several methods have been proposed for the measurement of the magnetic losses in electrical steel sheet in a rotating magnetic flux. The method considered here is based on determination of the field quantities and makes use of square specimens and an air gap between the pole faces and the specimen. We earlier reported the results of magnetic field analysis on this apparatus by the finite element method. In this paper we report a method for measuring rotational power losses together with measurement results.

articleTitle: Generating Mechanism of Magnetic Force in Meshing Area of Magnetic Gear Using Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new magnetic gear using a permanent magnet has been developed by the author. The design and performance characteristics of such magnetic gears have been reported previously. In this report, the mechanism by which magnetic force is generated in the meshing area is elucidated. An experimental meshing model is used to clarify the principle of operation of the magnetic gear. The meshing area consists of intersecting and main contact zones of the tooth profiles. In the intersecting zone, the negative magnetic force is clearly small and can be ignored when the intersecting tooth profile is larger than 8 degrees, as in the case studied.

articleTitle: High Frequency Characteristics of a Planar Inductor and a Magnetic Coupling Control Device
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on inductance calculations for a planar inductor and the characteristics of a magnetic coupling control device. First, the high frequency characteristics of a planar inductor, consisting of a meander coil and two magnetic films, was calculated using Neumann's formula and the reluctance method. The calculated value, taking the skin effect, proximity effect, eddy currents and stray capacitance into account, was in good agreement with the measured value. Second, a magnetic coupling control device was proposed as an application of a planar inductor. It consists of two meander coils and a magnetic film, which is inserted between the two coils. Experimental results show that the magnetic coupling between the two coils is changed by the magnetic film, and that it can be controlled by an external magnetic field.

articleTitle: Crystallization Behavior of Fe-M-C (M = Ti,Zr,Hf,V,Nb,Ta) Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Microcrystalline Fe-M-C (M = Ti,Zr,Hf,V,Nb,Ta) films crystallized from the amorphous state are suitable for use in magnetic heads. Crystallization of such films is supposed to be initiated by nucleation of fine carbides of the element M, because of the strong affinity of M for carbon. The precipitated Fe-rich phase was found to be a supersaturated solid solution with a tetragonally deformed lattice, and it gradually changes to the bec phase as the annealing temperature increases. In these alloys, the change in soft magnetic properties with annealing temperature seems to be strongly affected by grain size rather than by changes in crystal structure or magnetostriction. The coercivity increased at high annealing temperatures caused by grain growth of Fe. The upper limit to the annealing temperature is as high as 1000 K for Fe-Hf-C and Fe-Ta-C films, for which the crystallization temperature is relatively high.

articleTitle: Magnetooptic Current Field Sensor with Sensitivity Independent of Verdet Constant and Light Intensity
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new type of ac current sensor utilizing the Faraday effect is proposed. A stabilized dc bias magnetic field H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sup> is applied to a Faraday element placed between a crossed Nicols pair of polarizers. The amplitudes of the fundamental signal I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</sub> and second harmonic signal I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2ω</sub> induced by the ac field H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup> in the intensity of light emerging from the analyzer are phase-detected. The ratio R=I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2ω</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</sub> gives the output signal. When the Faraday rotation angles a (∝H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>) and θ (∝H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sup> are so small that such higher terms as a<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> can be neglected, we obtain R=H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>/4H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sup>, which is independent not only of the light intensity, but of the Verdet constant of the Faraday element as well. Experiments performed at 20 to 100°C on FR-5 glass and Bi-substituted YIG Faraday elements corroborated this prediction. The effect due to the nonlinear terms a<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is calculated, and found to agree with our experimental results.

articleTitle: Magnetic Recording Characteristics of Co Ferrite Perpendicular Anisotropy Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Spinel ferrite Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.10</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.90</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4 film of thickness 0.21 μm was prepared on a glass disk substrate by plasma-assisted MO-CVD using mixed vapor containing Fe(C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>7</sub>O<sub>2</sub>)<sub>3</sub>, Co(C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>7</sub>O<sub>2</sub>)<sub>3</sub> and O<sub>2</sub>. The film saturation magnetization and coercivity in the direction normal to the film plane at 8 kOe was 210 emu/cc and 1250 Oe respectively. X-ray diffraction patterns and SEM images of the film showed a columnar structure with a ≪100≫ preferred orientation. Magnetic recording tests were performed on the medium in disk form, using a MIG head of gap length 0.25 μm, at a relative speed of 9.4 m/s and a flying height of 0.1 μm. The recording density D50 was 15 kFRPI, and the reproduced waveform at 2.7 kFRPI had a dipulse shape indicating a perpendicular magnetization component.</sub>

articleTitle: Crystal Structure and Magnetic Properties of Mn-Al-Ni Ferromagnetic Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60-x</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> ternary films were prepared by dc magnetron sputtering and their crystallographic characteristics and magnetic properties were investigated. The τ phase was synthesized at Ni contents below 7 at%. The lattice constant a increased from 3.98 Å to 4.12 Å, and c decreased from 3.48 Å to 3.21 Å, as a result of increasing the Ni substitution. The M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of the τ-phase films increased with increasing Ni substitution up to an Ni content of a few percent. The maximum values for M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and Hc, 240 emu/cc and 2.9 kOe respectively, were obtained at an Ni content of 3 at%. The high H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> was due to the increased asymmetry of the tetragonal structure. The magnetic anisotropy of τ-phase films was caused mainly by the preferential orientation of the c-axis of the tetragonal crystallites.

articleTitle: Magnetovolume Effects of Fe Alloys: Magnetic Moment as a Function of Atomic Distance
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetovolume effects in 3d transition metal ferromagnets are reviewed. The mechanism of volume dependence of the magnetization is discussed on the basis of the itinerant electron theory of magnetism. Referring to the results of recent band calculations of bec and fcc iron as a function of atomic distance, quantitative estimations of the volume effects are given. The effect of chemical pressure on the magnetization of iron alloys is discussed together with other factors to determine the atomic moment.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Fe16N2 Films Prepared by Nitrogen Ion Implantation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Iron nitride films with large magnetization were prepared by nitrogen ion implantation into iron films. The saturation magnetization of the iron nitride films increased with increasing nitrogen concentration, and the highest value was obtained at the stoichiometric concentration of α"-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (11.1 at% N). X-ray analysis revealed that the iron nitride produced was composed of α'-martensite and α"-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. It was concluded that the increase in saturation magnetization was due not only to α"-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, but also to α'-martensite. The saturation magnetization of the iron nitrides was found to be 257 emu/g. Mössbauer spectra of the iron nitrides were fitted by three Fe sextets with hyperfine fields of 400, 325 and 290 kOe. The magnetic moment of Fe with the highest hyperfine field was estimated to be about 3.5 μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>.

articleTitle: Effects of Cu Addition on Bi-Substituted Garnet Film for Magnetooptical Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Polycrystalline Bi-substituted iron garnet films with Cu added were prepared on glass substrate by rf diode sputtering followed by annealing. The addition of 3.4 at% Cu was effective both for decreasing the size of crystallites to about 1 μm, and for increasing the coercivity to 5.4 kOe. The shape of statically recorded bits was also improved.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe16N2 Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Epitaxial growth of single-phase Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> single crystal films and the giant magnetic moment of such films are reviewed, along with partial formation of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> by implantation of N ions into Fe films. Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> single crystal (110) and (001) films have been grown epitaxially on Fe (001)/ In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>As (001) and on In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub> Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>As (001) substrates, respectively. Both films were found to have a saturation magnetic flux density Bs of from 2.8 T to 3.0 T (from 3.1μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> to 3.3μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> per Fe atom) at room temperature. This is in good agreement with the value (2.83 T) estimated by Kim and Takahashi from the Bs of polycrystalline Fe-N films consisting of Fe and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> crystallites. The origin of the giant magnetic moment is discussed on the basis of Mossbauer spectroscopy and calculations using the local density functional approximations of Sakuma.

articleTitle: Anomalous Behavior of Magnetization and Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy for Heusler Compound Type Multilayer Films, PtMnSb/CuMnSb
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayer films consisting of ferromagnetic PtMnSb and antiferromagnetic CuMnSb were prepared by a dual-type rf sputtering method. The thickness of a PtMnSb layer (d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Pt</sub>) was designed from 3.6 Å to 100 Å, holding the CuMnSb layer thickness constant at 100 Å. From X-ray diffraction data, all multilayer films were found to have a [111] texture of the C1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>-type Heusler structure. The magnetization of multilayer films showed anomalous behavior: 1) a great enhancement of the magnetization compared with that of a PtMnSb compound; and 2) a bend in the temperature dependence of the magnetization at about 50 K, near the Neel temperature of CuMnSb. The magnetization curve revealed that a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was induced with decreasing d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Pt</sub>. The interface contribution (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) and the volume contribution (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub>) to the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy were estimated to be K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> = 0.14 erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub> = -7.9 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of Sn-Substituted Mn2Sb Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Following our previous study on vacuum-evaporated Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb films with bismuth and chromium added, we have investigated the magnetic and magnetooptic properties of tin-substituted Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb (Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) films, with x varied from 0 to about 0.40 (13.2 at% Sn). Tin was chosen as the third element because there are two magnetic intermetallic compounds with different crystallographic structures in this system--Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb has a tetragonal structure, while Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sn has a hexagonal structure. As the amount of tin substitution increases, the diffraction lines from Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb become weak and the saturation magnetization decreases, but perpendicular magnetization films can nonetheless be obtained up to x=0.40. Results show that shrinking along the c-axis of the Mn≪≪MDSD≫≫2≪≪MDNM≫≫Sb lattice occurs in the vicinity of x=0.15 (5 at% Sn), at which a decrease in coercivity and increase in polar Kerr rotation are observed. These are considered to be closely related phenomena, presumably reflecting a change in the electronic structure of Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Microstructure of Electroless-Plated CoNiP Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The correlation between the magnetic properties and micro-structure of electroless-plated CoNiP perpendicular magnetic recording media was investigated. By adjusting the plating bath factors, the perpendicular coercivity, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub>, of the film can be controlled to up to 1500 Oe without changing the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and the shapes of the M-H loops. Reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) analysis showed that these films consist of mixtures of ≪002≫ perpendicularly oriented hep structure regions, and fcc regions without an obvious crystal orientation. The increase in the proportion of the ≪002≫ oriented hep region in such films results in higher H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> values; film with the maximum H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of 1500 Oe consisted almost entirely of ≪002≫ oriented hep crystal region. Transmission electron microscope observations revealed that the grain size increases to about 0.03 μm with an increase in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub>, up to 1500 Oe. It was also clarified that in the initial growth stage, these films show a low H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, and consist of fine crystallites with low crystal orientation.

articleTitle: Crystal Structure and Magnetic Properties of MnBiAI Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The properties of MnBiAl films prepared by alternately depositing, using vacuum evaporation, Mn and Bi layers with a single Al layer at the center, were studied. On annealing at temperatures between 230 and 420°C, films with Mn contents between 40 and 70 at% and with an Al content below 15 at% became ferromagnetic, with the magnetization perpendicular to the film plane. Adding Al caused the size of crystallites in the film to decrease to about 50 nm, and acted to suppress phase transitions between the low (Itp) and high (htp) temperature phases. Such films did not differ significantly from MnBi films with regard to the crystal structure, lattice constants or Curie temperature. The Kerr rotation spectrum had a maximum value of 1.78° at about 700 nm, as well as a peak value of 1.5° at 370 nm. Film reflectivities varied from 40 to 60% in the wavelength range from 330 to 800 nm.

articleTitle: Magnetooptic Effect of Fe-Ni, Ni-Co and Fe-Co Binary Alloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The longitudinal magnetooptic Kerr effect in evaporation-deposited Fe-Ni, Ni-Co and Fe-Co binary alloy films was measured in order to clarify the relationship between the magnetooptic Kerr effect and the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>. The results show that the relationship between the Kerr rotation θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> and M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> can be expressed as θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>∝M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> 1.7-2.1 at λ=400 to 1000 nm. The magnetooptic parameter Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, which is a measure of the magnitude of the magnetooptic effect, is not only dependent on the M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, but also on the crystal structure.

articleTitle: Magnetic Recording Properties of Double Layered Coating Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Double-layered particulate media were prepared with excellent magnetic recording characteristics over a wide frequency range. Video luminance signals were recorded only to a depth of 0.3 μm from the tape surface; however, video chrominance signals were recorded to a depth of 0.6 μm from the surface. By utilizing these characteristics, high-coercivity magnetic particles suitable for recording high-frequency signals can be used in the upper layer of the medium. However, performance is affected by the thickness of the upper layer and the coercive force of each layer. Hence these parameters should be chosen carefully, taking into account the recording depths of different signals.

articleTitle: Magnetization Reversal and Domain Wall Propagation Characteristics of Compound Magnetic Wire
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: When vicalloy wire (40 Fe-50 Co-10 V) is twisted, the outer areas in the wire, which undergo great stress as a result of twisting, take on a smaller coercivity. The pulse-inducing characteristics and domain wall propagation of such compound magnetic wire are described. It was found that the pulse voltage induced by large Barkhausen jumps is not proportional to the value of (H-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), where H is the critical field of domain nucleation at flux reversal and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the critical field of domain wall displacement. Moreover, H is decreased by applying a torsional stress to the wire.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy of CoOx Films Prepared by Targets Facing Type of Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin films with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) were prepared at room temperature by the reactive facing-target sputtering technique. We investigated the PMA, coercivity and static magnetization process of the film samples, with the following results. (1) CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> films with a columnar structure are composed of hep Co and fcc CoO. (2) The highest perpendicular anisotropy energy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> was 2.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> increases with increasing M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>; the PMA of CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin films is attributed to the magnetocrystalline anisotropy of Co. (3) Hca increases with decreasing diameter of columnar grains in CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin films. (4) The dependence of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> on the direction of the applied magnetic field is similar to that expected from the Stoner-Wohlfarth model. The static magnetization process in CoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin films is mainly the rotational type.

articleTitle: Development of Dental Magnetic Attachment with Rare Earth Magnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A dental magnetic attachment is a denture retainer with a permanent magnet. It has been suggested that such attachment possesses many advantages compared with conventional mechanical attachments, which often pose problems of retentive force durability as well as of esthetics. However, magnetic attachments have not been put into practical use because of the insufficient magnetic attractive force and because of corrosion of the magnet in the oral cavity. An advanced type of dental magnetic attachment has been developed with a sandwich-structuer magnetic circuit, in which a rare earth magnet is surrounded by a pair of yokes. The attachment generates a high attractive force of more than 4.9 N despite its small size. The magnet is sealed with a stainless steel cap, laser-welded to the yoke for perfect protection from corrosion.

articleTitle: Stress Measurement Using a Magnetic Anisotropy Sensor Utilizing AC Demagnetization
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic anisotropy sensor (MAS) is capable of non-contact measurement of the mechanical stress of ferromagnetic materials. This paper deals with the physical meaning of hysteresis phenomena in the MAS output voltage vs. stress characteristics of specimens (cold rolled steel). Experimental results revealed that the hysteresis of the MAS output voltage vs. stress characteristic is removed by the effect of ac demagnetizing at a field intensity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> about sixty times as large as the specimen coercivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>.

articleTitle: Preparation of Fe3O4 Films by Light-Enhanced Ferrite Planing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Polycrystalline Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> films were plated on glass substrates in an aqueous solution. By irradiating the substrate surface with an Xe lamp at power density of ~450 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the deposition rate of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> film was increased by a factor of about 10 (from ~30 nm/min to ~320 nm/min). With light irradiation times as short as 4 min, we obtained ferrite films of ~2 μm thickness. We believe that the light accelerates the reaction by raising the temperature. X-ray analysis revealed that the films were polycrystalline with a spinel structure, with no preferred orientation, and no scattering due to impurity phases was observed.

articleTitle: Effect of Initial Incident Angle on Magnetic Properties of Vacuum Deposited Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The incident angle dependence of the magnetic properties of vacuum-deposited Co-Cr films was investigated. Using a continuous vacuum deposition system, "continuous films" and "fixed films" were deposited onto polymer substrates in motion and held stationary, respectively, with the incident angle of evaporated atoms varying from 70° (initial) to 40° (final). In fixed films, which were cut into small pieces to perform measurements of regions in angular intervals of 2.5° the hep c-axis dispersion increases and the shape magnetic anisotropy increases with increasing angle of incidence. In continuous films, both magnetocrystalline anisotropy and shape magnetic anisotropy contribute to the magnetic anisotropy. Compared with fixed films, the magnetic properties of continuous films are influenced by the initial film growth region at incident angles above 60°.

articleTitle: Corrosion Analysis for Co-Ni-O Film Adopted as the Magnetic Layer of Metal Evaporated Tape
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Corrosion in Co-Ni-O film, which is adopted as the magnetic layer in metal evaporated tape media, was examined through aging tests, measurements of anode polarized characteristics, and analysis of both chemical bonding by ESCA and of crystallographic characteristics by RHEED. The following results were obtained. 1) The experimental results for exposure tests were strongly correlated with the anode characteristics. 2) Corrosion occurring in the uppermost layer of Co-Ni-O film exposed to high temperatures and high humidity progressed as follows: CoO+H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O→Co (OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, 2Co (OH)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>+0.5O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>→2CoOOH+H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O. 3) Both oxygen gas introduced in the deposition process, and fluorine lubricant coated onto the surface of the Co-Ni-O film give effective protection against corrosion.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magnetooptical Properties of Fe/V Compositionally Modulated Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic and magnetooptical properties of Fe/V compositionally modulated multilayer films (CMFs) prepared by rf sputtering were investigated. The crystallinity and periodicity of the Fe/V CMFs were inferior to those of Co/Pt, Fe/Pt, Co/Au and Fe/Au CMFs. The saturation magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) decreases rapidly with decreasing modulation length (D) below approximately 50 Å. Enhancement of the polar Kerr rotation angle (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>) such as appeared in Co/Pt and Fe/Cu CMFs was not observed. The shape of the θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> spectra is similar to the spectrum of Fe film, and shows no change even when D and the thickness ratio of Fe/V are varied. Moreover, the calculated θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> spectra are in good agreement with experimental results. This suggests that the interface layers in Fe/V CMF contribute insignificantly to the polar Kerr effect.

articleTitle: Effects of Underlayer on Magnetic Properties of CoNiCr Thin Film Media Sputtered on Glass Substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoNiCr/Cr films were sputtered onto polished glass at temperatures T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> ranging from 25 to 400°C, and their magnetic properties were investigated in connection with their micro-structure. H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> was found to increase with increasing T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> while sputtering GoNiCr/Cr films, which consisted mainly of an h.e.p. phase. Analytical transmission electron microscopy revealed that the underlayer Cr diffused into grain boundaries of the CoNiCr layer, and at higher T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, into individual CoNiCr grains. Torque loss analyses were performed to determine the magnetic isolation among CoNiCr grains. The uniaxial magnetic anisotropy field for individual grains determined experimentally, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">grain</sup> (exp), was found to increase with increasing Ts. Metalographical change promoted magnetic isolation among h.e.p. CoNiCr grains, and as a result, the microscopic demagnetizing field in each CoNiCr grain increased. This conclusion is well supported by the experimental results of the torque loss analysis in this work.

articleTitle: Magnetism of Interstitial Atoms in Transition and Rare-Earth Metals
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The ferromagnetic exchange splitting of the 3d electron band was found to play an important role in the physical nature of self-interstitial atoms in bec Fe. This effect is related to the problem of the large magnetic moment of Fe-N, in which the Fe-Fe atomic distance also plays an important role. The threshold energy for defect creation has been explained using a model d band in the series of transition elements. The anomalously low value for bec Fe is explained by considering the magnetic energy and the non-quenched orbitals of 3d band electrons. The interstitial migration temperatures of the transition metals, including the anomalously high value for bec Fe, are explained. The high interstitial migration temperature in rare-earth metals is also discussed in relation to the overlap of the 4f electron wave functions.

articleTitle: Mock Circulatory Test of Linear Pulse Motor-Driven Artificial Heart
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper deals with the characteristics of a linear pulse motor (LPM-S88) which was developed as a small-size electromagnetic actuator for a left-side artificial heart. The required thrust of the LPM of an artificial heart is calculated at 58.1 N. The maximum static thrust of the LPM-S88 using two-phase excitation is 94.2 N. An artificial heart driven by the LPM-S88 was capable of operating at 5.5 liters per minute at a pulse rate of 121 beats/min in a mock circulation test. Animal experiments using the artificial heart should be possible in the near future.

articleTitle: Effects of High Deposition Rate on Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media Prepared by SPT Target
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new sputtering source, called an SPT target, has been proposed, aimed at improvement of systems for continuous sputtering of Co-Cr double-layer perpendicular recording media. A very low discharge voltage was realized compared with sputtering source targets for magnetic media so far proposed. Both permalloy and Co-Cr films deposited using an SPT target had high crystal orientation even when fabricated at high deposition rates. High through-put (base film feed rates) during permalloy and Co-Cr layer deposition resulted in media with excellent recording density response, including a high 2nd peak ratio and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>* value. It was shown that the new SPT target is suitable for obtaining high through put in magnetic recording medium production.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of 6.5% Si Steel Sheets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Technology for the world's first production of 6.5% Si steel sheets in a coil form has been commercially developed. The dc and ac magnetostriction in 6.5% Si steel sheets and the noise in transformers employing such sheets were investigated, comparing the results with figures for conventional 3% Si steel sheets. 6.5% Si steel sheets had extremely small magnetostriction, and were found to be suitable for application in low-noise audio-frequency transformers.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Magnetic Properties of Silicon-Steel Sheet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of silicon steel sheet under conditions of two-dimensional excitation (circular, elliptic and alternating the rotation direction) were investigated. "Two-dimensional magnetic measurement" is a generic term introduced recently to describe the measurement of magnetic properties of a specimen under conditions of a rotating magnetic induction. The two-dimensional magnetic properties in silicon steel sheet are very sensitive to the axis ratio and the angle of inclination of the major axis of the induction, because they are very sensitive to the anisotropy of the material.

articleTitle: Magnetization Properties of YBaCuO Prepared by Quench and Melt Growth Process
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: DC magnetization measurements were carried out on YBaCuO prepared by the quench and melt-growth (QMG) process using a vibrating sample magnetometer and a SQUID magnetometer below 100 K. It was found that the DC magnetization behavior of QMG-grown YBaCuO at 4.2 K can be quantitatively explained in terms of Bean's critical state model. This sample also can become a strong bulk permanent magnet with an energy product of more than 80 MGOe at 5 K because of its strong pinning force.

articleTitle: Mechanism of Magnetic Curtain Produced by Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The present paper focuses on the mechanism of magnetic curtains. The pressure of gas flowing near a magnetic curtain was measured. Flows of gases such as nitrogen and oxygen were supplied to an air gap between the magnetic poles, and the differential pressure was measured with a manometer. It was found that the tendency of the magnetic curtain to block the gas flow can be classified into three general regions, according to the flow velocity. When the flow velocity is low, gas leaks out of the magnetic curtain (region 1). When the flow velocity is moderate, the gas flow is blocked (region 2). When the flow velocity is high, the gas flow is pinched in passing through the magnetic curtain (region 3). Based on experimental results, a model of magnetic curtains was introduced, and a magnetic curtain was simulated.

articleTitle: Preparation of CoB Soft Magnetic Thin Films by Eleetroless Plating
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Eleetroless plated CoB films were plated in a bath with dimethylamineborane (DMAB) as a reducing agent. The magnetic properties of films changed widely with changes in the concentration of the complexing agent in the bath, such as ammonium sulfate or sodium tartrate. Film with the lowest coercivity was obtained from the bath containing 0.3 mol/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of sodium sulfate and 0.55 mol/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of sodium tartrate. Structural analysis of this film by electron microscopy revealed that the film consists of fine, highly crystalline particles with the hep structure.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Compositionally Modulated Fe/Al Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe/Al compositionally modulated multilayer films were prepared at a low argon pressure of 2 mTorr by double-target dc magnetron sputtering. The low argon pressure resulted in formation of films with minute grain sizes and a low H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. For a constant Al layer thickness of 8 Å, the alloy phase at the interfaces of the Fe/Al layers has a substantial effect on the apparent measured properties of films with an Fe/Al layer thickness ratio of less than 3, resulting in a decreased saturation magnetization with decreasing Fe/Al thickness ratio. At higher Fe/Al thickness ratios, however, the saturation magnetization remained nearly constant. The lowest H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> was obtained at an Fe/Al thickness ratio of around 3. Films with the optimum preparation parameters of Fe/Al thickness ratio=3 and modulation wavelength=43 Å exhibited the following properties: H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>=0.625 Oe, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>=1285 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, ρ=60 μΩ-cm.

articleTitle: Effect of Preferred Orientation on Magnetoresistive Properties of Fe/Cr Multilayers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe/Cr multilayer films were prepared by an alternating deposition technique in ultra-high vacuum on MgO (100), glass, and sapphire (0001) substrates. Giant magnetoresistive changes were observed in the three kinds of multilayer films. Films on glass substrate had a poly-crystalline structure and showed a `magnetoresistive change of 8.4% at room temperature and 26.4% at 77 K under applied magnetic fields of up to 7 kOe. Sharp and flat interfaces result in a larger magnetoresistive change. Epitaxial growth on GaAs (100) substrate is not essential for producing the giant magneto-resistivity.

articleTitle: Various Factors Affecting Eddy Current Distribution of Single Sheet Testers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It has been pointed out that the error in the power loss measured by a single sheet tester is mainly due to eddy currents in the specimen. The eddy current distribution is affected by the yoke construction, the overhang of the specimen, the distance between the yokes, and other factors. We previously reported on the effect of the yoke construction. In this paper, the effects on measurement error of the specimen overhang and the distance between yokes are examined both experimentally and through numerical analysis by the 3-D finite element method.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Modulation Recording on GdDyFeCo Magnetooptical Disk

articleTitle: Characteristics of Multilayer Eddy-Current Type Coil with Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes a new multilayer coil with a core for generating high ac magnetic fields. The new device employs an eddy current-type multilayer coil in which the core is set to decrease the exciting current. The core always operates in an unsaturated state. The device efficiently concentrates ac magnetic flux and makes it easier to obtain a high magnetic field. The structure and characteristics of the device are also discussed.

articleTitle: Improvements of Coercivity and Corrosion Resistance in Nd-Fe-Co-B Sintered Magnet by Addition of V or Mo
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structure, magnetic properties and corrosion resistance of sintered anisotropic Nd-Dy-Fe-Co-B- (V or Mo) permanent magnets are reported. Addition of a few atomic percent V or Mo was found to be beneficial in that it enhances the intrinsic coercivity (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cJ</inf>) without significantly sacrificing the remanence or maximum energy product, especially when a substantial amount of Co (approximately 5 at%) is present. Thus the addition of V or Mo together with Co serves to improve both corrosion resistance and temperature stability of the magnetic properties. Possible reasons for the enhancement of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cJ</inf>by V and Mo are also discussed.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Pd/Co Multilayered Films with Various Buffer Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Pd/Co multilayer films were prepared by rf sputtering, with a buffer layer of Pt, Pd, Cu or SiAlON between the multilayer film and the glass substrate. The type of buffer layer was found to have an effect on the structure as well as the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and coercive force of the multilayer film. A Pt buffer layer improves the layer structure and ≪111≫ orientation, as well as increasing the anisotropy, while SiAlON and Cu do not improve the layer structure but do increase the coercivity.

articleTitle: Rotational Dynamic Magnetostriction of Si-Fe Sheet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Rotational dynamic magnetostriction (RDM) was measured as a function of rotating magnetic flux density for nonoriented and grain-oriented silicon steel sheets under various magnetizaiton conditions. The rotational dynamic magnetostriction was measured using two-dimensional strain gauges, which provide x- and y-directional outputs. The RDM in silicon steel sheet is larger than the alternating magnetostriction in the rolled direction.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Amorphous CoNbZr/AlN Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of the magnetic properties of multilayer CoNbZr/AlN films on the conditions of film preparation was investigated. AlN films were prepared by N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reactive sputtering deposition on CoNbZr films. The soft magnetic properties of the as-deposited films were found to be strongly related to the rf input power during AlN deposition. The anisotropy field decreases drastically at an input power of greater than 2 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a high permeability of around 10,000 (at 5 MHz) was obtained for as-deposited films prepared at an rf input power during A1N deposition of 4.4 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. SEM observations revealed that CoNbZr films in as-deposited multilayer form have nearly the same morphology as amorphous alloy films annealed at the optimum temperature for reduction of the anisotropy field. The annealing process during film preparation (self-annealing effect) is attributed to the heat generated during AlN deposition, originating mainly in the heat of formation in AlN reactive sputtering.

articleTitle: Effects of Addition of Zr and Ti on Sputtered Fe-N Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of addition of Zr and Ti on iron films containing nitrogen were investigated. Film structures and magnetic properties were studied as functions of the Zr and Ti contents. The coercive force of Fe-N films increased sharply after annealing at about 350°C, while Fe-Zr-N and Fe-Ti-N films retained a small coercive force even after annealing at higher temperatures. The addition of Zr and Ti in small amounts was highly effective in improving the thermal stability of Fe-N because it prevented the growth of iron crystal grains.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of Magnetooptical Media with Auxiliary Magnetic Layer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the leakage field from the auxiliary layer to the recording layer in an exchange-coupled multilayered magneto-optical medium. In order to estimate the leakage field, test media, in which the auxiliary layer was deposited on the recording layer with a nonmagnetic layer intervening, were prepared. The leakage field was determined as the difference in the threshold external fields for two different initial magnetization directions in recording tests. The experimental results were in good agreement with numerical calculations, in which single-domain nucleation was assumed. The leakage field was found to be proportional to the change in magnetization at the heated spot. It was also found that a leakage field of about 200 Oe is generated in the auxiliary layer with a change in magnetization of 150 emu/cc.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Performance of Soft Heating Element for Local Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The soft heating method is an induction heating method utilizing temperature-sensitive magnetic materials implanted in the body. In this method, the Curie temperature is the reference temperature and the generation of heat is controlled automatically. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of three kinds of soft heating elements: a temperature-sensitive ferrite rod, which is a hybrid device, ferrite powders, and temperature-sensitive Fe-P-C-Cr amorphous metal flakes. The ferrite rod can be applied to treatment of tumors in the rectum or vagina, and the amorphous metal flakes to deep-seated tumors.

articleTitle: Effects of Magnetic Head Wear on Envelope
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The signal envelope reproduced by a VCR head varies depending on the combination of the magnetic head contour shape and the tape stiffness, and particularly with low-stiffness tapes which result in a damped envelope. The shapes of head sliding surfaces were measured by the interference ring method using spline interpolation. Changes in the head shape due to wear resulted in various patterns depending on the head construction. The dependence of reproduced envelopes on the head shape and tape tension was studied in connection with the tape stiffness. The reproduced envelope was found to decrease with increasing radius of curvature of the head surface in the width direction. The envelope can be improved by choosing the best gap position on the head contour for different head constructions, and by decreasing the tape tension and head protrusion.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Magnetoresistance and Hall Effects for Ni-Co Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relationship between anisotropic magnetoresistance and the Hall effect was studied for fcc Ni-Co binary alloy thin films. The maximum value of Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> was 5.3%, obtained for 75 at % Ni-Co alloy. At this alloy composition, the ordinary Hall coefficient R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> was -2.0×l0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">~12</sup> V- cm/A-Oe, and the extraordinary Hall coefficient R3 was 0.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> V-cm/A-G, or very nearly zero. It was also found that the magnetic moment per atom was 0.9μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>LB at this same alloy composition. All these relationships were found to be nearly the same as for Ni-Fe alloys. These results suggest that a large value of Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> can be obtained in fcc Ni-base alloys under the following conditions: (1) when R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is negative-valued and its absolute value is large, (2) when R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is close to zero, and (3) when the magnetic moment per atom is 0.9μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>.

articleTitle: Irradiation Effect of Ion Beam in FexN Films Prepared by IRD
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic thin films of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N were prepared by so-called "ion reacting deposition." To clarify the effect of ion beam irradiation during deposition, the difference between use of N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ions and Ar ions was studied. A low-energy broad-beam ion source (Kaufman type) was directed normal to the substrate, which was set obliquely to the direction of iron vapor incidence. All of the Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N films consisted mainly of paramagnetic ε-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-3</sub>N and α-Fe according to Mossbauer measurements; that is, separation into two phases took place in these films. The coercive force H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of iron films prepared by Ar ion beam irradiation decreased with increasing ion current density, while that of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N films increased to saturation. This indicates that the ion bombardment did not lead to the increase in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. We were able to analyze the film magnetic anisotropy into two different shape anisotropies related to the columnar microstructure of the film. The change in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and shape anisotropy in Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N films can be attributed to the anisotropy in the packing density of α-Fe, as estimated from the observed saturation magnetization of the films.

articleTitle: A Discussion about Soft Magnetic Properties of Highly Oriented Fe-Base Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: I-H loops of ≪111≫, ≪100≫ and ≪100≫ oriented single-crystal films of Fe-base alloys were obtained by calculations in which the single-domain model was used, with the total energy including the shape anisotropy, magnetocrystalline anisotropy and magnetic field energy. These calculations show that the coercive force of ≪111≫ oriented film is as small as 50 A/m, less than one one-hundredth of that for ≪110≫ and ≪100≫ oriented film. In addition, the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> (magnetic anisotropy constant) dependence and shape dependence of the coercive force for ≪111≫ oriented film were obtained.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy of fcc-Fe/Cu MBE Ultra Thin Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayered and sandwiched ultra-thin fcc-Fe/Cu films were prepared on Cu (100) by the MBE method. The epitaxial growth of films was observed by RHEED, the periodicity of the multilayered films was confirmed by X-ray diffraction, and film magnetization was measured. All fcc Fe films on Cu (100) exhibited ferromagnetism, and the magnetic moment of an Fe atom was estimated to be 2.0±0.2 μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>. The Curie temperature of the fcc Fe was above room temperature (578±5 K for [10ML Fe/10ML Cu]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>), and depended oh the number of Fe atomic layers. Films with fewer than three monolayers of Fe exhibited perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of Single Pole Thin Film Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The recording characteristics of single-pole thin film heads were investigated. Both a narrow track and a high linear recording density are necessary for high areal density recording. Single-pole thin film heads with the main pole thickness varied between 0.15 μm and 1.1 μm were trial-manufactured, and the recording characteristics were examined using a Co-Cr-Pt/Ni-Fe perpendicular magnetic recording medium. At a main pole thickness of 0.2 μm, a C/N ratio of 41 dB, media noise of 2.4 μV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</sub> and overwrite level of -30 dB were confirmed.

articleTitle: Dynamical Magnetic Field Analysis of Motor by Remesh Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic field analysis techniques have been widely applied to the optimal design of magnetic circuits as the key components of electric devices. This paper describes a new numerical approach to complicated dynamical systems in which the magnetic field changes with time and with movement of objects, and demonstrates application to an induction motor. This method is based only on finite element analysis, without taking into account the modification of boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Influence of Head Fields and Media Properties on Transitions of Magnetization Reversals on Thin Film Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes a relationship between transition lengths and head fields for media of various coercivities. Signals with various transition lengths were written using a single-sided and a double-sided MIG head on three different thin film media, of coercivity 874, 1121 and 1270 Oe. The transition lengths were observed by the colloid SEM method. The head fields of the MIG heads were analyzed by the finite element method (FEM) with magnetic saturation taken into account. The following phenomena were discovered: (1) the secondary fields stray from the saturated ferrite region near the interface between the metal film and ferrite core of the MIG heads; (2) the transition lengths are elongated due to the influence of the secondary field when the strength of the secondary field is greater than half of the medium coercivity. On the other hand, if the medium coercivity is twice as great as the secondary field strength, then the transition length is closely related to the field gradient of the primary field in the recording zone.

articleTitle: Effects of Oxygen on Magnetic and Magnetooptical Properties of PtMnSb Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of oxygen in Ar/O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixed sputtering gas on the magnetic and magnetooptic properties of PtMnSb films prepared by rf sputtering were investigated. In addition to a PtMnSb phase, the growth of Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb, PtSb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and oxides of Mn and Sb were observed in PtMnSb films prepared at low total sputtering gas pressures. The saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> decreases with decreasing total gas pressure, leading to improvement in the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of films. The change in the Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Kp</sub> with decreasing total gas pressure is small compared with the change in M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, and μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Kp</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is increased at low total gas pressures.

articleTitle: Preparation and Magneto-Optical Properties of Metal Fine Particles Dispersed in Liquid
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe, Ni, Cu and MnSb fine particles were prepared at various Ar pressures (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> to 5.0 Torr), and were dispersed in a liquid (arkylnaphthalene with 10 vol% surfactant). The mean diameter of Fe particles increased from 20Å to 180Å, and that of MnSb particles from 160Å to 280Å, as the Ar pressure under which particles were prepared was increased. Fe and Cu particles included oxides, and MnSb was decomposed to Mn and Sb when the pressure was low. The Faraday rotation θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> of these liquids was measured for various particle concentrations. The θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> decreased with decreasing particle concentration. These results are in good agreement with values calculated assuming that particles are dispersed homogeneously and do not interact with each other.

articleTitle: Magnetooptical Recording with Optical Modulation and Magnetic Field Modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetooptic recording characteristics of three types of DyFeCo films with a quadrilayer structure were measured using three recording methods: optical modulation, magnetic field modulation and the laser-off method. In the laser-off method, the laser power was lowered only while the magnetic field was changing. The transition metal (TM)-rich medium had the best carrier-to-noise (C/N) ratio when using the optical modulation method. When using magnetic field modulation, the C/N was lower than for optical modulation recording. The three media had similar characteristics when using magnetic field modulation. Adoption of the laser-off method improved the C/N and the magnetic field dependence of the C/N. In particular, the TM-rich medium exhibited the same C/N as when using optical modulation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy and Magnetooptical Property of TbFe/SiO Compositionally Modulated Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic anisotropy of a TbFe/SiO compositionally modulated film was studied. The magnetic anisotropy energy increases with the number of TbFe layers. The magnetic interaction between the TbFe layers contributes to the magnetic anisotropy even when the distance between the TbFe layers is 10 nm or more. Measured magnetic properties and ESCA analyses of annealed samples showed preferential oxidation of Tb. The energy spectra of the Si 2p electron indicate the coexistence of SiO and pure Si. The concentration of pure Si becomes greater at interfaces than at the centers of layers. Reduction of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> on annealing can be compensated by combining TbFe layers with different Fe concentrations, some Tb-rich and others Fe-rich.

articleTitle: Behavior of Hysteresis in Magnetostrictive Torque Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The hysteresis behavior of magnetostrictive torque sensors was investigated. Various kinds of steel were applied to driving shafts with sets of parallel grooves. Single magnetostrictive output (mode I, II output) obtained from tensile and compressive stress, and differential output obtained from differentiated mode I, II output, were observed. The mode I, II output was nonlinear and asymmetric; however, the differential output was linear and symmetric. It was found that mode I, II output characteristics may be classified according to the shaft material and heat treatment, and that the hysteretic behavior of the differential output can be predicted by assuming combinations of these types of characteristics.

articleTitle: Effect of Magnetic Properties for High Density Recording of Barium-Ferrite Particulate Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In this paper we introduce barium ferrite tape samples with a high recording characteristic in the conventional longitudinal magnetization mode, and explain the origin of their high output voltage at high recording densities, with reference to the effect of the magnetic characteristic and the behavior of remanent magnetization. Longitudinally and non-oriented barium ferrite recording media were prepared using the same magnetic paint based on a single barium ferrite magnetic particle. The barium ferrite tapes thus prepared were inferior to ultra-high density metal tapes with regard to surface roughness and magnetic energy, but exhibit better recording characteristics at high recording densities above 80 kFRPI or so. In particular, the origin of the high recording characteristic of longitudinally oriented barium-ferrite tape samples may be explained by the effect of the sample remanence curves, rather than by perpendicular magnetization.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Al-Si/Fe Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports on the magnetic properties of Fe-Al-Si/Fe multilayer films prepared by rf sputtering. As-deposited Fe-Al-Si/Fe multilayer films have a high saturation flux density of 16 kG and an initial permeability of more than 1000, even though the initial permeability of single-layer Fe-Al-Si film is less than 500. As-deposited Fe and Fe-Al-Si single-layer films of thickness less than 1000 Å have good soft magnetic properties. The soft magnetic properties of the multilayer films are improved by annealing, which acts to relieve the internal stress. The thinner the individual layers of the film, the better are the soft magnetic properties of the film. Fe-Al-Si (50Å)/Fe (50Å) multilayer films annealed at 400 to 450°C exhibit a low coercivity of 0.7 Oe and a high initial permeability of 4000.

articleTitle: Crystallographic Orientation and Magnetic Properties of Fe-O and Fe-O-N Films Deposited by ECR Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Oxygen was introduced into the Ar sputtering atmosphere during deposition of iron films. It was found that oxygen dramatically enhances the [100] orientation of the iron films, while no sign of oxide formation was found in X-ray diffraction patterns, X-ray photoelectron spectra, or measured magnetic properties. Films deposited with nitrogen introduced together with oxygen during sputtering were also studied. Results revealed that even a small amount of nitrogen prevents the iron film from assuming the [100] orientation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Stimulation of the Brain and Spinal Cord by a Pair of Opposing Pulsed Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method of localized stimulation of the human brain and spinal cord is proposed. The basic idea is to concentrate induced eddy currents locally in the vicinity of a target by a pair of opposing pulsed magnetic fields. A figure-of-eight coil was designed, and magnetic stimulation of brain and spinal roots were carried out. The results show that the functional mapping of the human motor cortex related to the hand, arm and foot areas can be obtained. Experiments using rabbits were carried out to verify the usefulness of magnetic stimulation of the spinal cord in detail. Selective stimulation of each spinal segment from outside of the body was possible. It was also found that the amplitude of the EMG signals varies with the direction of the stimulating currents.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Characteristics of Transcutaneous Thin Transformer Utilizing Amorphous Magnetic Fiber for Implantable Artificial Heart
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper deals with the characteristics of a thin disk-shaped transformer utilizing amorphous magnetic fiber, designed for an artificial heart system. The transformer can be applied to the patient with the primary coil placed on the surface of the body and the secondary coil implanted subcutaneously. There was little leakage flux behind the coils and relatively small change in output power with relative coil displacement. The system could transmit over 100 W of electric power. When transmitting 20 W, the temperature rise of the secondary coil was about 7.5°C, and efficiency was about 90%.

articleTitle: Reliability in Head-Disk-Interface with Negative Pressure Slider
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The head-disk interface of a negative-pressure slider is evaluated. The damage occurring on seeking and tracking is caused by dust invading the space between the slider and the disk and wearing down the disk surface. Such damage is suppressed by controlling the cleanliness and wear resistance of the disk surface. The slider does not make contact with the disk even at a flying height of 0.1 μm, because damage does not occur under conditions of high cleanliness. The environment cleanliness and disk surface wear resistance (environment stress) were varied in accelerated lifetime tests; the results indicated that the interface has a long lifetime of over 300,000 hours. In start/stop operation using loading/unloading, the slider sustained no damage in over 30,000 cycles.
